cells.tense: A clear eye is opening, and you are here while it opens.
cells.act: go all the way into the pattern until you meet its edge
cells.ask: Follow a read you trust as far as it goes — a judgment about a person, a call about your work — until thinking stops. Stop at that edge and notice where it fell.
cells.core:
A clear eye is opening, and it's yours. Not a flash this time — something that holds. You look at a situation and it shows itself as it is, and the showing feels like it was there before you arrived, which is how you can tell it's steady. The fairness you keep is doing its work: when something sits crooked you feel it, and when it sits true you feel that too. Nothing in you is arguing about what's on the table.

Follow a read you trust as far as it goes. A judgment about a person, a call about your work, the shape you think something has. Go with it to the point where thinking stops. Stop at that edge and notice where it fell. The depth you're after doesn't come from more opinions; it comes from going past the comfortable middle of something you already hold. One read, taken to its edge, shows you more than ten fresh ones would.

cells.tense: A clarity is coming, and you will have your answer ready before it can arrive.
cells.act: let what was only possible stand finished
cells.ask: Take a thing that turns up this week and sit with it as plain as it is, without turning it into a verdict. Let it stay unfinished. Don't dress it up.
cells.core:
The new seeing is coming, and you're ahead of it. Tomorrow's read is already formed, so what's here now doesn't get to speak first. You answer questions nobody has asked yet, and the answers arrive sounding like things you've actually seen, which is the trouble. The eye is real. The reach has gotten past it. What's here is small and fresh; what you're saying is large and settled.

Take a thing that turns up this week and sit with it as plain as it is, without turning it into a verdict. Let it stay unfinished. What you're practising is the difference between the read and the report about the read. Not to be modest — for the sake of the eye. A beginning stays a beginning only if you let it. Otherwise the first cut happens in your head and lands somewhere already shaped, and you don't find out what was actually here.

cells.tense: A clear eye opened and you walked past it, and you're still standing at that door.
cells.act: complete the form so it stands without you
cells.ask: Finish a thing you saw and set down — a repair, a revision, a note you meant to send. Do it in a sitting, no explaining, and let it hold where it can be seen.
cells.core:
Something showed itself plainly and nothing came of it. The eye opened and you kept walking, and the walking has had time to become a habit. Now the present is thin — things arrive and you don't quite meet them — and the balances you keep for other people aren't being kept for your own hour. You can still spot what sits crooked across a room. You just don't bring that eye home. This isn't a failure of sight. What was seen was set down somewhere and the finishing part has gone quiet.

Finish a thing you saw and set down. A repair. A revision. A note you meant to send. Do it in a sitting, no explaining, and let it hold where it can be seen. What arrives then isn't the feeling of having seen well — it's the habit of bringing what you see into a form that holds. One form, standing without you, is where the current returns.

cells.tense: A clear eye has been working in you and the account of it belongs to others.
cells.act: meet what is arriving as it arrives
cells.ask: Catch a thing as it turns up — a face, a tone, a request — and note it before you note what it means. One sentence of plain notice, then nothing more.
cells.core:
The clear sight is happening. You're doing it. Ask anyone who was there the last time you walked into a room and they'll tell you a read, a summary, something you caught that nobody else did. Ask what your part in it was and you'll say it was obvious, that the read was just there. The eye works through you and your words leave you out. This is how fairness usually gets described — as if proportion were found rather than made. Your version has you arriving at the scene instead of looking at it.

Catch a thing as it turns up — a face, a tone, a request — and note it before you note what it means. One sentence of plain notice, then nothing more. That gap is the part that belongs to you. Not the whole account of the moment; just the split second in which a thing registers as itself. Catch the moment the read is yours, and let that stand where it can be seen.
